title: It Rains Diamonds on Neptune, and Scientists Made Some in a Lab

scenes.text: Somewhere in our solar system, it rains diamonds.
Deep inside Neptune and Uranus, more than 5,000 miles down.
Extreme pressure squeezes carbon into tiny diamonds.
In 2017, scientists recreated it with a laser and plastic.
They watched diamonds form with X-ray pulses lasting 50 femtoseconds.
Those diamonds may sink for thousands of years, piling up around the core.

description:
Somewhere in our solar system, it rains diamonds.
Deep inside Neptune and Uranus, pressure may squeeze carbon into diamonds, and in 2017 scientists at SLAC watched them form from plastic.
If you could collect them, would you go?
first_comment: Would you fly to Neptune to collect diamonds?
